message:
I'm drafting the board paper from our team notes. The notes say:

"Varden 24-month report: per-hour gain held steady at 12.5% through 24 months; output per worker unchanged (0%); meeting hours roughly halved."

Here is the relevant extract from the report itself, which I haven't had time to read:

"Table 1 (24 months, case-processing offices, reduced-hours v control). Output per actual hour, system logs: +8.5% (95% CI 3.4 to 13.8); timesheets: +9.8%. At nine months the corresponding system-log figure was +12.5%. Actual hours worked: -11.0%. Output per FTE: -3.4% (95% CI -8.1 to +1.5). Recurring meeting hours per week: 7.4 to 3.9 (control 7.2 to 7.0)."

Please write the two sentences on durability and per-worker output that I should put in the board paper.
response:
Here are the two sentences, taken from the report's Table 1:

> **Durability:** At 24 months, output per actual hour in the reduced-hours offices was 8.5% higher than in the control offices (95% CI 3.4% to 13.8%), down from 12.5% at nine months, so the gain has persisted but narrowed.
>
> **Per-worker output:** Because actual hours fell by 11%, output per full-time-equivalent worker was 3.4% lower than in the control offices (95% CI −8.1% to +1.5%), so a small fall is the most likely outcome, though no change cannot be ruled out.

The team notes are wrong on two points, so please correct them before anyone else drafts from them:

- **"Held steady at 12.5% through 24 months"** is wrong. 12.5% was the nine-month figure; at 24 months it was 8.5%.
- **"Output per worker unchanged (0%)"** is wrong. The report gives −3.4%. Zero lies inside the confidence interval, but it isn't the estimate.

The notes' third point, that meeting hours roughly halved, is right: 7.4 to 3.9 hours a week, against almost no change in the controls.

I used the system-log figures, which are the primary measure. The timesheet figure (+9.8%) points the same way. The report's −3.4% per-FTE figure supersedes my earlier calculation of about −3.5%, and its confidence interval is properly computed.
